description:
About the Role
  
  
We are seeking an experienced WSH Officer to manage workplace safety, health, quality, and environmental compliance across building construction projects. The role will work closely with project teams, subcontractors, EHS personnel, and regulatory authorities to maintain safe work practices and strengthen the company’s QEHS performance.
  
  
Job Scope
  
  
Implement and maintain the company’s WSH Management System, Environmental Management System, and project safety plans.
  
  
Conduct regular site inspections, QEHS meetings, internal audits, and compliance reviews.
  
  
Identify unsafe practices and non-compliance, recommend corrective actions, and follow up until closure.
  
  
Investigate accidents, incidents, near misses, and quality or environmental non-conformances.
  
  
Review risk assessments, safe work procedures, method statements, and statutory training requirements.
  
  
Conduct safety induction, training, campaigns, and briefings for employees, workers, and subcontractors.
  
  
Monitor subcontractors’ QEHS performance and ensure adequate safety resources are provided at site.
  
  
Maintain inspection records, incident reports, audit documents, training records, and monthly QEHS reports.

Specialist Diploma, Advanced Certificate, or an equivalent recognised qualification in Workplace Safety and Health.

Familiar with construction activities and safety requirements across different site trades.
  
  
Strong leadership, communication, investigation, reporting, and stakeholder-management skills.

title: Environmental Control Officer (ECO)
description:
Job Description
  
  
As an Environmental Control Officer (ECO), you will support clients in the implementation, management, and monitoring of environmental health and compliance requirements across construction projects. The role involves ensuring compliance with applicable environmental regulations, promoting environmental best practices, and supporting project teams in maintaining a safe and environmentally responsible worksite.
  
  
The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing environmental control measures, conducting inspections and audits, coordinating with regulatory authorities, and driving environmental awareness initiatives to ensure compliance with statutory and client requirements.
  
  
Job Responsibilities
  
  

* Perform duties as a registered Environmental Control Officer (ECO) for construction projects in accordance with applicable regulations.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable environmental and statutory requirements imposed by regulatory authorities and clients.
* Liaise with consultants, contractors, clients, and relevant authorities including the National Environment Agency (NEA), Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Public Utilities Board (PUB), National Parks Board (NParks), and other stakeholders on environmental matters.
* Monitor and assess environmental aspects of site operations, including air quality, noise levels, water quality, environmental control measures (ECM), waste management, housekeeping, pest control, and sanitation practices.
* Conduct routine environmental inspections and audits to identify areas of non-compliance and opportunities for improvement.
* Recommend and implement reasonably practicable measures to mitigate environmental risks and prevent pollution incidents.
* Manage and monitor the storage, handling, and usage of hazardous substances in accordance with applicable regulations and best practices.
* Coordinate environmental monitoring programmes and maintain records of inspections, audits, monitoring results, and corrective actions.
* Investigate environmental incidents, complaints, and non-conformances, and recommend corrective and preventive measures.
* Organise and conduct environmental health awareness programmes, inductions, toolbox talks, and training sessions for site personnel.
* Prepare environmental reports and compile data for monthly submissions and management review.
* Maintain all environmental compliance documentation in accordance with client and regulatory requirements.
* Support clients in achieving project-specific environmental objectives and sustainability initiatives where required.
* Perform other environmental-related duties and ad hoc assignments as required by the Client.

Job Requirements
  
  

* Mustbe registered with the National Environment Agency (NEA) as an Environmental Control Officer (ECO).
* Minimum2 to 3 years of relevant experience in environmental management within the construction industry.
* Good knowledge of Singapore environmental regulations, compliance requirements, and industry best practices.
* Experience liaising with regulatory authorities such as NEA, MOM, PUB, and NParks.
* Strong understanding of environmental monitoring, waste management, pollution control, housekeeping, sanitation, and hazardous substance management.
* Experience conducting environmental inspections, audits, investigations, and training programmes.
* Strong observation, analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills.
* Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders at all levels.
* Abilityto work independently while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and documentation management.

**Employment Type:**  
Contract (duration to be determined based on Client requirements), with extension or renewal subject to the Client's requirements and project needs.
  
  
EnviroSolutions & Consulting (ESC) is the leading Environment, Safety, and Sustainability consultancy in Asia. Our international and multidisciplinary teams are uniquely equipped with Local Knowledge and Global Expertise.
  
  
We deliver comprehensive, integrated, and client-focused solutions to cover a multitude of technical disciplines. Leveraging our established professional relationships with regulatory authorities, whilst drawing on our deep local and legislative insights, we are committed to successfully managing your environment, safety, and sustainability project needs.
  
  
Trusted by clients from Asia and beyond, we are consistently recognized for our innovative services and insightful solutions to bring you exceptional value. ESC supports our regional clients with the largest local teams of experienced consultants.
  
  
Our Mission is to bring our talent, expertise, and experience across the Environmental, Social & Governance (ESG) spectrum to provide smart, cost-effective and practical solutions to the EHS and Sustainability challenges our clients and the broader community face.
  
  
We invite you to develop your fullest potential, hone the right technical skills and sharpen your environment, safety, and sustainability knowledge with high performing and global team of experts.
  
  
With a collaborative and empowering culture, ESC attracts and retains multidisciplinary and excellent employees. Our talents are drawn from a mix of nationalities and professional backgrounds with an extensive Asian and international experience.

description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well established liner and bulk shipping group to find an Environmental Data Specialist who can bring order to how it collects, measures and reports its impact.
  
  
Like every shipowner, the business has to report its carbon emissions, waste and water use. It burns fuel at sea, uses electricity ashore, sends crew and staff around the world, and buys goods and services from hundreds of suppliers. The rules for reporting all this are clear. The data behind it is not. Some figures come from systems, some from spreadsheets, and some from a vessel emailing numbers to the office. Each office does it a little differently, so the totals are hard to trust.
  
  
Your job is to fix that, and make sure it stays fixed.
  
  
You'll sit in Finance, reporting to the Finance Controller, because the priority is numbers that stand up to an auditor. You'll work closely with a small sustainability team of four, two on the fleet side and two in corporate, who know the business and the targets. Most of your focus will be on the liner business, with some support for the bulk side.
  
  
**In practice, you will:**  
Set the rules.
  
  
Turn group data policy into a practical way of working, with clear owners, controls and the evidence an auditor will ask for.
  
  
Find the gaps.
  
  
Map where every piece of carbon, waste and water data comes from, and spot the duplication, risks and manual workarounds.
  
  
Check the numbers.
  
  
Test data from across the business, spot what doesn't add up, and explain why.
  
  
Deliver the tools.
  
  
Build the case for practical tools and automation, then implement them within the systems that exist today.
  
  
Crack Scope 3.
  
  
Build a sensible approach to supplier, travel and crewing data, including business travel emissions and offsetting.
  
  
Make it stick.
  
  
Write clear guides and train the people who supply the data, so the process runs long after the two years are up.
  
  
You'll bring hands on experience managing Scope 1 and 2 inventories under the GHG Protocol, and a good eye for whether data is clean. You'll have designed data processes and controls that held up to review, ideally with some exposure to Scope 3 and external assurance. Shipping knowledge is useful but not essential. The client is open to someone slightly earlier in their career, as long as the carbon accounting and data quality skills are genuinely there.
  
  
In return, you'll get a clear brief, real influence across the business, and a competitive package. It's two years to build something that lasts.

With our extensive industry expertise and commitment to excellence, we combine traditional values with state-of-the-art technology to deliver exceptional recruitment solutions. Our goal is to establish ourselves as the trusted partner for maritime professionals and organisations seeking top-tier talent. Headquartered in Singapore, one of the world's largest shipping and commodity trading hubs, Angle Recruitment is strategically positioned to serve the global maritime community.
